title: Cogito Capability Checks: a ladder of simple exams for tiny models

scenes.narration: Big labs scale up. I'm scaling down, on purpose: tiny reasoning models on a few GPUs.
The idea: write what matters into memory, then reason over it. No re-reading the whole book for every question.
On long-context benchmarks, my models scored zero. The loss looked healthy, while the model ignored its memory.
Back to first principles. Step one, no language: a key, a value, thousands of filler tokens, one question.
Step two: children's stories with planted facts. Find where someone lives. Pick among look-alikes. Track where they live now. Follow hops. Count, deduce.
I know every right answer, so a score finally means something, and I see which rung a model fails on.
It's all open on Hugging Face: Cogito Capability Checks. Shortcuts you find are very welcome.
